2026:UHC:8408
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Anticipatory Bail Cancellation Application No. 05 of 2025
Kashmir Singh ....Applicant
Versus
Ashok Khurana and Another ....Respondents
Present:-
Mr. Hari Om Bhakuni, Advocate for the applicant.
Mr. Pankaj Joshi, A.G.A. for the State.
Mr. M.S. Pal, Senior Advocate assisted by Ms. Amreen Bano, Advocate for
the respondents.
Hon'ble Ravindra Maithani, J. (Oral)
Respondent nos. 1 and 2, Ashok Khurana and Ankur
Khurana ("the accused") respectively were granted ad interim
anticipatory bail by this Court on in Anticipatory Bail Application
No.1159 of 2023, Ashok Khurana and Another v. State of Uttarakhand
on 28.12.2023, which was finally confirmed on 24.07.2024. Now, the
informant of the case has sought cancellation of the anticipatory bail
granted to the accused.
2. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the
record.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the
accused had played fraud with the Court; the trial court had already
issued Non Bailable Warrants and process under Section 82 of the
Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 ("the Code") against the accused, but
this fact was concealed before the Court, and it was also wrongly stated
that a civil suit was pending on the date when the anticipatory bail was
heard by the Court, wherein, it is argued that on the date when the

2
anticipatory bail application of the accused was heard and decided, no
civil suit was pending. It is argued that the anticipatory bail order, so
obtained, deserves to be cancelled.
4. Learned Senior Counsel appearing for the accused
submits that insofar as the accused Ankur Khurana is concerned, he
has nothing to say because he has already left abroad, but insofar as
the accused Ashok Khurana is concerned, it is argued that, in fact, in
the instant case, the FIR was lodged on 03.10.2015, when a Civil Suit
No.1 of 2015, Ashok Khurana v. Smt. Braj, was pending between the
parties, which was finally dismissed on 21.10.2021. It is argued that no
fraud was played with the Court while applying for anticipatory bail by
the accused. At it, learned counsel for the applicant submits that the
civil suit was filed on 10.10.2015.
5. Anticipatory bail, once granted, cannot be easily
cancelled unless there are reasons to do so. According to the FIR, in the
instant case, the accused Ashok Khurana was made caretaker of a
premises, but subsequently, he was removed and the applicant, who is
the informant in the case, was appointed as caretaker. But,
subsequently, the accused Ashok Khurana claimed that he is tenant in
the premises, and it was done by him by forging lease deed.
Subsequently, FIR was lodged against the accused and others.
6. The question is as to whether any fraud was played
with the Court? Or any such statement was given, which was false and
which may have the consequence of cancelling the anticipatory bail
granted to the accused?
7. At the time of hearing, learned State Counsel gives a
statement that insofar as the accused Ankush Khurana is concerned,

3
he is absconding. His file has already been consigned after separating
from the main file, and there is a permanent warrant issued against
him. Therefore, there is no question of cancelling the anticipatory bail
granted to the accused Ankush Khurana because his anticipatory bail
already stood cancelled, as he has absconded.
8. Insofar as the accused Ashok Khurana is concerned, in
the bail cancellation application, in Para 28 itself, the applicant writes
that in C482 No.1588 of 2017, on 13.12.2023, Non-Bailable Warrants
and process under Section 82 of the Code that were issued against the
accused Ashok Khurana, was quashed. It means, post 13.12.2023,
there were no Non Bailable Warrants or process under Section 82 of the
Code against the accused Ashok Khurana. Had the factum of issuance
of Non Bailable Warrants and process under Section 82 of the Code
been concealed while granting bail, the situation would have been
different, but in the instant case, for the first time, ad interim
anticipatory bail was granted on 28.12.2023, and it was confirmed on
24.07.2024. On both these dates, Non-Bailable Warrants and process
under Section 82 of the Code were not in existence. Therefore, it cannot
be said that any concealment on that aspect was done.
9. Insofar as statement with regard to pendency of civil
litigation between the parties is concerned, it is true that it was argued
on behalf of the accused that there had been civil litigation pending
between the parties, and a fact, which was admitted by learned State
Counsel when anticipatory bail applications were heard. It is a fact that
after the FIR was lodged, there was a civil suit pending between the
parties, which was Civil Suit No.1 of 2015, in the court of Civil Judge,
Senior Division, Nainital. Although, it has already been dismissed much

4
before the anticipatory bail was granted. But, this Court does not see
that it is a fraud. The fact that there was a dispute with regard to the
property and parties were in litigation is true. Therefore, on this score
also, this Court is of the view that there is no reason to cancel the
anticipatory bail granted to the accused Ashok Khurana.
10. Having considered, this Court is of the view that there is
no reason to make any interference, and there is no reason to cancel
the anticipatory bail granted to the accused Ashok Khurana.
Accordingly, the anticipatory bail cancellation application qua accused
Ashok Khurana deserves to be dismissed.
11. The anticipatory bail cancellation application is
dismissed qua accused Ashok Khurana.
 (Ravindra Maithani, J.)
 18.09.2026
Ravi Bisht
